caption:
A bookcase hid eight people from the Nazis for two years and still swings open today — and a single flower bulb once sold for more than an Amsterdam canal house. 👀

Comment your guess for which fact surprised you most before you swipe ⬇️

1. Anne Frank House
In 1942, a helper built a revolving bookcase to hide the entrance to the Secret Annex — the only way in or out for the eight people hiding behind it. It's still there, and still swings open today.

2. Royal Palace
Built on marshland in the 1600s, the Royal Palace on Dam Square rests on 13,659 wooden piles driven deep into the soil. Locals called it the Eighth Wonder of the World when it opened as a town hall.

3. Begijnhof
Step through an unmarked gate off a busy shopping street and find the Begijnhof — a silent medieval courtyard hiding the city's oldest surviving wooden house, built around 1528.

4. Canal houses
Amsterdammers were once taxed by how wide their house was along the canal, so houses were built narrow and tall instead. Furniture still goes in through the windows using the hoisting hooks on the gables.

5. Tulip Mania
During Tulip Mania in 1637, one rare tulip bulb sold for more than an Amsterdam canal house. It's considered the world's first recorded market bubble — and it collapsed just as fast as it rose.

6. The canal ring
Amsterdam holds 165 canals and over 1,700 bridges, all entirely man-made. That's more waterways than Venice — built to drain the marshland the city sits on, not for gondolas.

7. Bikes in the canals
Amsterdam holds the Guinness World Record for bicycles fished out of a city's waterways. Claw-armed barges haul roughly 15,000 out every year, mostly stolen or dumped.
